look_here_first: TUMBLEGRASS (long treated as Schedonnardus paniculatus) has a DISTINCTIVE architecture: a low tuft with long, often stiff curved flowering axis and several long, very slender, widely diverging one-sided racemes. On a mature raceme, spikelets sit in TWO ROWS along one side of the axis. Look at the whole branch pattern FIRST; then confirm that unilateral spikelet arrangement and membranous ligule. Old dry heads may detach and tumble.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Tumblegrass long divergent one-sided racemes are not the densely packed panicle of Lindheimer, nor the short narrow contracted panicle of nimblewill. Sideoats grama bears MANY short pendent lateral spikes along a flowering axis rather than a few long thin stiff racemes. Purple lovegrass has a diffuse branching cloud with spikelets dispersed on very fine branches, not distinctive straight unilateral racemes.

what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Full rooted low tuft showing long flowering culm and several widely diverging racemes.
Close photograph down ONE mature raceme showing sessile spikelets arranged in two rows on its one side.
Leaf blade showing spiral twisting or white margins with ruler.
Membranous ligule and a dissected one-flowered spikelet with a millimeter scale.
Mature detached tumblegrass seedhead and intact attached head to teach what tumbles.
morphology_keys.crew_identification_guardrails: The long widely spreading flowering racemes are photographable; their microscopic one-sided spikelet arrangement and detachment are not proven by the current photograph.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Tumblegrass: look for long spreading racemes
steps: START with the physically archived Matt Lavin photograph: trace the long slender divergent branches arising from a curved central flowering axis, rather than mistaking each branch for an independent flowering stem.

ON A FRESH BRANCH inspect one side of the branch axis: the narrow spikelets are held appressed along one side (secund / unilateral), generally one fertile floret each. The existing photo shows the branch architecture, but its resolution is not proof of counted florets.

LOOK AT THE BLADE–SHEATH JUNCTION with a 1-mm ruler and 10–20× magnification. Under the Schedonnardus treatment Kew describes an ECILIATE MEMBRANOUS ligule (no fringe of long marginal hairs). Do not place a ligule arrow on the overview photo.

CHECK a mature intact 3–4 mm spikelet with a 1-mm ruler: identify two glumes and the single fertile lemma. Source morphology describes a narrow laterally compressed spikelet; the current images do not prove those measurements.

COMPARE the curved axis, alternate spreading lateral branches and tightly aligned spikelets with any superficial windmill-grass lookalike. One-sided aligned sessile spikelets, not just a windmill silhouette, are the confirmation target.
KEEP FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until a real source-verified same-plant Texas branch macro, ligule and dissected spikelet are archived and reviewed.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Curved flowering axis + long widely spreading one-sided slender branches + appressed unilateral spikelets; confirm an eciliate membrane ligule and single-flowered spikelet at scale.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: The two archived source-labelled photographs show inflorescence architecture, not a magnified blade/sheath junction or dissected spikelet. The searched Commons files were either already installed or distant habitat views; no redundant photo was installed on 2026-10-23.
